Source text: Parents: LM 13-LP3 x LM 14-LP4. Gazette Notification: S.O.4065 (E) Dated 31.08.2022. Season: Kharif. Maturity: Long (95-100 days). Yield: 9.0 to 10.0 t/ha. Moderate resistant (MR) to major diseases of north western plains zone (NWPZ) namely maydis leaf blight (MLB) and charcoal rot (ChR). Variety name: CO 6
Crop: Maize
Category: Field Corn
Type: Hybrid
Developer or company: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (TNAU)
Parents: (UMI 1200 x UMI 1230)
Growing season: Adipattam (July–August); Purattasipattam (September–October); Thaipattam (January–February)
Maturity class: 110 days
Minimum maturity days: 110.0
Maximum maturity days: 110.0
Yield: 7400 irrigated; 5000 rainfed
Yield unit: kg/ha grain
Normalized yield minimum: 50.0
Normalized yield maximum: 74.0
Recommended regions: All maize-growing areas (Tamil Nadu CPG context)
Irrigation condition: Rainfed and irrigated
Stem borer response: Moderately resistant
Turcicum leaf blight response: Resistant
Maydis leaf blight response: Resistant
Banded leaf sheath blight response: Resistant
Downy mildew response: Resistant
Grain type: Semi-dent
Grain colour: Orange-yellow
Special traits: High starch (76.30%), protein (11.25%), beta-carotene (0.48 mg/100g), moderate fat (4.65%), crude fibre (1.25%), high shelling (81%) and test weight (400 g/1000 seeds); easier hybrid seed production through synchronized flowering.
Source text: TNAU CPG 2012 maize profile: TNAU maize hybrid CO 6; parentage (UMI 1200 x UMI 1230); duration 110 days; all maize-growing areas; rainfed and irrigated; grain yield 7,400 kg/ha irrigated and 5,000 kg/ha rainfed. Special features: starch 76.30%, protein 11.25%, beta-carotene 0.48 mg/100g, fat 4.65%, crude fibre 1.25%, shelling 81%, test weight 400 g/1000 seeds; multiple disease resistance to sorghum downy mildew, Maydis leaf blight, Turcicum leaf blight, post-flowering stalk rot and banded leaf and sheath blight; moderately resistant to stem borer; parent flowering can be synchronized by sowing at the same time. Grain: orange-yellow, semi-dent. Recommended in Adipattam (July–August), Purattasipattam (September–October) and Thaipattam (January–February).
